The incidence of cancer in dogs is significantly elevated compared to humans—lymphoma occurs 2~5 times more often, mammary cancer 4 times, osteosarcoma 8 times, and skin cancer 35 times more frequently in dogs. For dogs aged 8 and older, the cancer incidence rate approaches 40~50%. Despite the growing market for pet medications, the development of new veterinary drugs has not kept pace with demand.
